### 1.  The tangency condition

Fix a smooth conic \(C_{0}\).  
Write a variable conic as the zero–locus of a quadratic form  

\[
Q(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Ax ,\qquad A=(a_{ij})\in \operatorname{Sym}_{3}.
\]

\(C\) is tangent to \(C_{0}\) iff there exists a point
\(p\in\mathbf P^{2}\) such that  

\[
Q_{0}(p)=0,\qquad Q(p)=0,\qquad \nabla Q_{0}(p)\ \text{and}\ \nabla Q(p)
\ \text{are linearly dependent}.
\]

Eliminating the point \(p\) gives a single homogeneous equation of
degree 2 in the coefficients of \(A\); consequently the set

\[
T_{C_{0}}=\{\,C\in\mathbf P^{5}\mid C\text{ is tangent to }C_{0}\,\}
\]

is a **quadric hypersurface** of \(\mathbf P^{5}\).  
(One can obtain the same conclusion by computing the resultant of the
two quadrics; the resultant is a homogeneous polynomial of degree 2 in
the coefficients of the second quadric.)

Thus for each smooth conic \(C_{i}\;(i=2,\dots ,6)\) we obtain a quadric
\(Q_{i}\subset \mathbf P^{5}\) consisting of the conics tangent to
\(C_{i}\).

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 2.  The fibre of \(\pi\)

Let \((C_{2},\dots ,C_{6})\in U^{5}\) be a generic tuple of smooth
conics.  The fibre \(\pi^{-1}(C_{2},\dots ,C_{6})\) is precisely the
intersection

\[
Q_{2}\cap Q_{3}\cap Q_{4}\cap Q_{5}\cap Q_{6}\subset \mathbf P^{5}.
\]

Each \(Q_{i}\) is a quadric, they are in general position for a generic
choice of the \(C_{i}\)’s, and the intersection is zero‑dimensional.
By Bézout’s theorem the degree of the intersection equals the product of
the degrees of the hypersurfaces:

\[
\deg\bigl(Q_{2}\cap\cdots\cap Q_{6}\bigr)=2^{5}=32 .
\]

Hence a generic fibre consists of **exactly 32 distinct geometric
points**, i.e. 32 smooth conics tangent to the five given smooth conics.

\(Z\subset U^{6}\) is defined by the five tangency equations, so
